newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish inflationary expectations soften - survey.
newsitem.headline: Swedish inflationary expectations soften - survey.

text.p: Sweden's business sector has lowered its inflationary expectations to the point they stand below central bank goals, a survey commissioned by the Riksbank showed on Wednesday.

In its third survey this year, economic research institute Prospera AB found money market players, purchasing managers, employees' and employers' organisations now on average saw inflation at an annualised 1.7 percent in a year's time.
This compared with expectations of 2.3 percent, a year ahead, at the last poll in May.
The survey found expectations of inflation at 1.9 percent in two year's time compared to 2.4 percent two years ahead at the last poll, and in five years at 2.2 percent against 2.7 percent.
"The inflationary expectations the next year and the next two years are thereby below the Riksbank's inflationary goal of two percent," Prospera said in a statement.
"For the five years to come the inflationary expectations fall within the bank's upper tolerance limit of three percent for all interviewee categories.
"All changes between the two surveys can be regarded as statistically significant."
Prospera said the survey found interviewees believed in a smaller average increase in the Consumer Price Index in coming years than they did in May.
The researcher said all those surveyed had basically the same opinion of how inflation will develop over the next five years. All believed in successively increasing inflation.
Wage increase expectations for the coming years have also been lowered with the exception of the employees' one year and two year assessments.
On average those questioned saw wages in one year rising 3.3 percent compared to expectations of 3.6 percent in May.
In two years, wages were seen rising 3.2 percent against 3.5 percent in May and in five years 3.3 percent against 3.5 percent in the earlier poll.

The employees' group, however, expected wages to rise 4.1 percent in one year compared to expectations of 4.0 percent in May. In two years they forecast wages rising 3.9 percent against 3.8 percent in the previous poll.
The survey of 360 people is conducted by Prospera on behalf of the Riksbank four times a year.
It is one of the central bank's key analytical tools used in its policy planning and is considered one of the weightiest in Sweden when it comes to forecasting inflation.
The Riksbank's next inflation report is due September 24.
